title: Mathematics Practice Test 2 - Mathematics - Statistics (Expected Value)
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Cameron’s bookshelf has 3 books with a rating of 10, 5 books with a rating of 100, and 2 books with a rating of 70. There are no other books on the bookshelf. What is the expected value, to the nearest whole number, of the rating of a book randomly selected from Cameron’s bookshelf?
questions.explain: The expected value is the sum of each outcome multiplied by its probability, which is the same as finding the overall average of the ratings in this context. The total number of books is $3 + 5 + 2 = 10$. The total rating points sum to: $3(10) + 5(100) + 2(70) = 30 + 500 + 140 = 670$. Dividing the sum by the total number of books: $670 / 10 = 67$.
